headline: South Korea says seven financial companies have now had customer information stolen in simultaneous hacking attacks, and regulators ordered emergency security checks across the whole sector.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a national-scale financial breach with regulators and the president involved; AI use is only suspected.
importance_line: Customers and businesses of the affected banks face leaked contact details, and regulators are pressed to defend the whole sector; officials say AI use cannot be ruled out but have not shown that AI was used.
summary: SBS News reports that the number of South Korean banks and credit firms confirmed hit by data leaks has risen to seven, with Welcome Savings Bank newly added after about 2,200 pieces of corporate customer information, such as names, emails and phone numbers, are estimated to have leaked. The Financial Services Commission chairman said the use of AI in the attacks cannot be ruled out, and banks and card companies must finish emergency inspections by 6 Oct 2026, with other institutions to follow by 8 Oct.
notes: Follows the 3 Oct pool item on the police probe into the same wave of bank hacks.
